name: Citric acid
what_it_is: A sour-tasting acid found naturally in lemons and limes. The kind used in food is made industrially by fermenting sugar with a mould.
why_its_added: Gives a sour taste, keeps colour from fading, and makes it harder for microbes to grow.

india.note: Maximum level depends on the food. Examples below.

eu.note: Scientific Opinion on the safety evaluation of the active substances citric acid -E330- and sodium hydrogen carbonate -E500ii-, used as carbon dioxide generators, together with liquid absorbers cellulose and polyacrylic acid sodium salt crosslinked, in active food contact materials.

usa.note: Generally Recognised As Safe (GRAS) for direct addition to food (21 CFR 184.1033)

safe_daily_limit.no_number_means: EFSA has not set a number for this one. That can mean it is considered safe enough not to need a limit, or that the evidence was not sufficient to set one. The opinion itself says which.

means: No single-serving limit has been found for this substance. That is not the same as there being no risk from one large serving - it means nobody has published a number.

people_reports.rule: Reports are shown as reports. We count them. We never turn them into a health claim, and we never let them change the sourced facts above.
